q: The radius and height of a right circular cone are in the ratio 3 : 4. If its curved surface area (in cm 2 ) is 240π. Then its volume (in cm 3 ) is:
s: r : h = 3 : 4 $$l$$ : r = 5 : 3 $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Curved surface area}} = \pi rl \\ & 240\pi = \pi \times 3x \times 5x \\ & {x^2} = 16 \\ & x = 4 \\ & \therefore r = 3 \times 4 = 12 \\ & {\text{Volume}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \frac{1}{3}\pi \times 144 \times 16 \\ & = 768\pi \end{aligned}$$

q: A cylindrical pencil of diameter 1.2 cm has one of its end sharpened into a conical shape of height 1.4 cm. The volume of the material removed is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Required volume removed}} \\ & = \pi {r^2}h - \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \frac{2}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times .6 \times .6 \times 1.4 \\ & = 1.056{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: A sphere and a hemisphere have the same volume. The ratio of their curved surface area is:
s: Let the radius of hemisphere and sphere be 'r' and 'R' $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{3}\pi {R^3} = \frac{2}{3}\pi {r^3} \\ & \frac{{{R^3}}}{{{r^3}}} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & \frac{R}{r} = \frac{1}{{\sqrt[3]2 }} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{Ratio of curved surface area}} \\ & = \frac{{4\pi {R^2}}}{{2\pi {r^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{2{R^2}}}{{{r^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times 1}}{{{{\left( {\sqrt[3]2 } \right)}^2}}} \\ & = \frac{2}{{{{\left( 2 \right)}^{\frac{2}{3}}}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{R}{r} = \frac{{{2^{\frac{1}{3}}}}}{1} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tank 40 m long, 30 m broad and 12 m deep is dug in a field 1000 m long and 30 m wide. By how much will the level of the field rise if the earth dug out of the tank is evenly spread over the field?
s: Volume of earth taken out = 40 × 30 × 12 = 14400 m 3 Area of rectangular field = 1000 × 30 = 30000 m 2 Area of region of tank = 40 × 30 = 1200 m 2 Remaining area = 30000 - 1200 = 28800 m 2 Increase in height $$= \frac{{14400}}{{28800}} = 0.5{\text{ m}}$$

q: A tank is in the form of a cuboid with length 12 m. If 18 kilolitre of water is removed from it, the water level goes down by 30 cm. What is the width (in m) of the tank?
s: Volume of cuboid = $$l$$bh 12 × b × h - 18 = 12 × b × (h - 0.3) 12bh - 18 = 12bh - 3.6b b = 5 m

q: A solid brass sphere of radius 2.1 dm is converted into a right circular cylindrical rod of length 7 cm. The ratio of total surface areas of the rod to the sphere is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3}\pi {R^3} = \pi {r^2}h \\ & \frac{4}{3}\pi \times 21 \times 21 \times 21 = \pi \times {R^2} \times 7 \\ & {R^2} = 21 \times 21 \times 4 \\ & R = 42{\text{ cm}} \\ & \frac{{{\text{total surface area of rod}}}}{{{\text{total surface area of sphere}}}} \\ & = \frac{{2\pi r\left( {h + r} \right)}}{{4\pi {R^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{42\left( {42 + 7} \right)}}{{2 \times 21 \times 21}} \\ & = \frac{{49}}{{21}} \\ & = \frac{7}{3} \\ & = 7:3 \end{aligned}$$

q: A solid cylinder has radius of base 14 cm and height 15 cm. 4 identical cylinders are cut from each base as shown in the given figure. Height of small cylinder is 5 cm. What is the total surface area (in cm 2 ) of the remaining part?

q: A cylindrical vessel whose base is horizontal and is of internal radius 3.5 cm contains sufficient water so that when a solid sphere is placed inside, water just covers the sphere. The sphere fits in the Cylinder exactly. The depth of water in the vessel before the sphere was put, is
s: Height of water after ball is immersed = 3.5 × 2 = 7 cm $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {\text{Volume of water}} = \pi {r^2}h - \frac{4}{3}\pi {r^3} \\ & = \pi {r^2}\left( {h - \frac{4}{3}r} \right) \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5\left( {7 - \frac{4}{3} \times 3.5} \right) \\ & = 11 \times 3.5\left( {\frac{7}{3}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{269.5}}{3}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of water before ball was immersed $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \pi {\left( {3.5} \right)^2} \times h = \frac{{269.5}}{3} \\ & h = \frac{{269.5 \times 7}}{{3 \times 3.5 \times 3.5 \times 22}} \\ & h = \frac{7}{3}{\text{ cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A hemispherical depression of diameter 4 cm is cut out from each face of a cubical block of sides 10 cm. Find the surface area of the remaining solid (in cm 2 ). $$\left( {{\text{Use }}\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)$$
s: Side of cubical block = 10 cm ∴ Area of each face of cubical block = 10 2 = 100 cm 2 Radius of Hemisphere = $$\frac{4}{2}$$ = 2 cm Surface area of hemisphere $$\begin{aligned} & = 2\pi {r^2} \\ & = 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times {2^2}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \frac{{176}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ Total surface area of hemisphere $$= 6 \times \frac{{176}}{7} = \frac{{1056}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2}$$ Remaining surface area of each face of cubical block $$\begin{aligned} & = {10^2} - 2\pi r \\ & = 100 - 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 2{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 100 - \frac{{88}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \frac{{612}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Total surface area of 6 remaining cubical block $$= 6 \times \frac{{612}}{7} = \frac{{3672}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2}$$ ∴ Surface area of remaining solid $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{1056}}{7} + \frac{{3672}}{7}} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \frac{{4728}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 675\frac{3}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The lateral surface area of frustum of a right circular cone if the area of its base is 16π cm 2 and the diameter of circular upper surface is 4 cm and slant height 6 cm, will be
s: Base Area = 16π πR 2 = 16π R = 4 Given r = 2 n ∆ABC ≅ ∆ADE $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{{\text{BC}}}}{{{\text{DE}}}} = \frac{{{\text{AC}}}}{{{\text{AE}}}} \\ & \frac{4}{8} = \frac{6}{{{\text{AE}}}} \\ & {\text{AE}} = 12 = {\text{L}} \end{aligned}$$ Surface Area of frustum = πRL - πr$$l$$ = π × 4 × 12 - π × 2 × 6 = 48π - 12π = 36π

q: A semi-circular sheet of metal of diameter 28 cm is bent into an open conical cup. The depth of the cup is approximately
s: Radius of semi-circular sheet = r ⇒ $$\frac{{28}}{2}$$ r = 14 cm Circumference of sheet = πr = 14π cm Sheet is folded to form a cone Let radius of cone = r 1 ∴ The circumference of base of cone ⇒ Circumference of sheet ∴ 2πr 1 = 14π r 1 = 7 cm ∴ Radius of cone = 7 cm Slant height = Radius of semi-circular sheet r = 14 cm $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{Height}} = \sqrt {{{\left( {14} \right)}^2} - {{\left( 7 \right)}^2}} \\ & = \sqrt {147} \\ & = 12{\text{ cm}}\,\,\,\left( {{\text{approx}}} \right) \end{aligned}$$

q: A hemispherical tank full of water is emptied by a pipe at the rate of 7.7 litres per second. How much time (in hours) will it take to empty $$\frac{2}{3}$$ part of the tank, if the internal radius of the tank is 10.5 m?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 7.7{\text{ Ltr/sec}} \\ & r = 10.5{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{V}} = \frac{2}{3}\pi {r^3} \times \frac{2}{3} \\ & = \frac{{\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 1000}}{{7.7 \times 60 \times 6000}} \\ & = \frac{{20 \times 105}}{{36}} \\ & = \frac{{175}}{3}{\text{ hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The base of a cone and a cylinder have the same radius 6 cm. They have also the same height 8 cm. The ratio of the curved surface of the cylinder to that of the cone is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Slant height of the cone }}\left( l \right) \\ & = \sqrt {{6^2} + {8^2}} \\ & = 10{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{Required ratio}} = \frac{{2\pi rh}}{{\pi rl}} \\ & = \frac{{2h}}{l} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times 8}}{{10}} \\ & = 8:5 \end{aligned}$$

q: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 264 m 2 and its volume is 924 m 3 $$\left( {{\text{Taking }}\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right).$$ Find the ratio of its diameter to its height
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 2\pi rh = 264{\text{ }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \pi {r^2}h = 924{\text{ }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{On dividing}}:\frac{{2\pi rh}}{{\pi {r^2}h}} = \frac{{264}}{{924}} \\ & \frac{2}{r} = \frac{{264}}{{924}} \\ & r = \frac{{924 \times 2}}{{264}} \\ & r = 7{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{Diameter}} = 2r = 2 \times 7 = 14{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{Putting, }}r = 7{\text{ in equation }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & 2\pi rh = 264 \\ & h = \frac{{264 \times 7}}{{2 \times 22 \times 7}} \\ & h = 6{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{Required ratio}} = \frac{{2r}}{h} = \frac{{14}}{6} = \frac{7}{3} \end{aligned}$$

q: A solid has 12 vertices and 30 edges. How many faces does it have?
s: In a solid by Euler's formula Faces + Vertices - 2 = Edges ⇒ Faces + 12 - 2 = 30 ⇒ Faces = 30 - 10 = 20

q: The diameter of a 120 cm long roller is 84 cm. It takes 500 complete revolutions of the roller to level a ground. The cost of levelling the ground at Rs. 1.50 sq. m. is:
s: According to the question, Diameter = 84 cm Radius = 42 cm = 0.42 m Height = 120 cm = 1.2 m CSA of cylinder = 2πrh $$= 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 0.42 \times 1.2$$ Total area covered to planed in 500 rounds $$\begin{aligned} & = 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 0.42 \times 1.2 \times 500 \\ & {\text{Total cost}} = \left( {2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 0.42 \times 1.2 \times 500} \right) \times 1.50 \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}2376 \end{aligned}$$

q: A cuboidal shaped water tank, 2.1 m long and 1.5 m broad is half filled with water. If 630 litres more water is poured into tank, the water level will rise
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 2.1{\text{ m}} \times 1.5{\text{ m}} \times h = 630{\text{ lt}} \\ & \frac{{21}}{{10}}{\text{m}} \times \frac{{15}}{{10}}{\text{m}} \times h = \frac{{630}}{{1000}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ \[\left[ \begin{gathered} \because 1\,{{\text{m}}^3} = 1000{\text{ lt}} \\ {\text{1000 c}}{{\text{m}}^3} = 1{\text{ lt}} \\ \end{gathered} \right]\] $$h = \frac{1}{5}{\text{m}} = 0.20{\text{ metre}}$$

q: The radii of two circular faces of the frustum of a cone of height 10.5 cm are 5 cm and 3 cm respectively. What is its volume in cm 3 $$\left( {\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)?$$
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{V}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left( {{R^2} + {r^2} + Rr} \right)h \\ & {\text{V}} = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7}\left( {25 + 9 + 15} \right) \times 10.5 \\ & {\text{V}} = 11 \times 49 \\ & {\text{V}} = 539{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A wall 12 m long, 9 m high and 90 cm thick is to be constructed. Given that one pack contains 450 bricks, how many packs of bricks will be required if each brick is of dimensions 10 cm × 7.5 cm × 7 cm and the cement and sand mixture occupies one-eighteenth volume of the wall? (Rounded off to the nearest integer)

q: A sector of radius 10.5 cm with the central angle 120° is folded to form a cone by joining the two bounding radii of the sector. What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the cone so formed?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Length of Arc}} = L \\ & L = 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{r \times 120}}{{360}} \\ & L = 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 10.5 \times \frac{1}{3} \\ & L = 22 \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & 2\pi R = 22 \\ & 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7}R = 22 \\ & R = 3.5 \\ & {h^2} + {R^2} = {10.5^2} \\ & {h^2} + {3.5^2} = {10.5^2} \\ & h = 7\sqrt 2 \\ & V = \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & V = \frac{1}{3}\pi \times 3.5 \times 3.5 \times 7\sqrt 2 \\ & V = \frac{{343\sqrt 2 }}{{12}}\pi \end{aligned}$$

q: A sphere of diameter 6 cm is dropped in a right circular cylindrical vessel partly filled with water. The diameter of the cylindrical vessel is 12 cm. If the sphere is just completely submerged in water, then the rise of water level in the cylindrical vessel is:

q: A solid cube has side 8 cm. It is cut along diagonals of top face to get 4 equal parts. What is the total surface (in cm 2 ) of each part?

q: The base of a right pyramid is a square of side 8√2 cm and each of its slant edge is of length 10 cm. What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the pyramid?

q: The base of a solid right prism of height 10 cm is a square and its volume is 160 m 3 . What is the total surface area of the prism (in cm 2 )?

q: A solid lead sphere of radius 11 cm is melted and recast into small solid spheres of radius 2 cm each. How many maximum number (in integer) of such spheres can be made?

q: A hemisphere is kept on top of a cube. Its front view is shown in the given figure. The total height of the figure is 21 cm. The ratio of curved surfaces area of hemisphere and total surface area of cube is 11 : 42. What is the total volume (in cm 3 ) of figure?

q: The internal measure of a cuboidal room are with length as 12 m, breadth as 8 m and height as 10 m. The total cost (in Rs.) of white washing all four walls of the room and also the ceiling of the room, if the cost of white washing is Rs. 25 per m 2 is:

q: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 4 cm, its surface area is increased by 464π cm 2 . What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the original sphere?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 4\pi \left[ {{{\left( {R + 4} \right)}^2} - {R^2}} \right] = 464\pi \\ & 4\left( {R + 4 + R} \right)\left( {R + 4 - R} \right) = 464 \\ & 16\left( {2R + 4} \right) = 464 \\ & 2R + 4 = 29 \\ & R = \frac{{25}}{2} \\ & {\text{Volume of sphare}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi {R^3} \\ & = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( {\frac{{25}}{2}} \right)^3} \\ & = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{15625}}{8}\pi \\ & = \frac{{15625}}{6}\pi \end{aligned}$$

q: Which of the following two will provide more volume? I. A cuboid of edges 6 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm II. A cube of edge 7 cm

q: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 2310 cm 2 and its radius is 21 cm. If its radius is increased by 100% and height is reduced by 50%, then its capacity (in litres) will be (correct to one decimal place): $$\left( {{\text{Take }}\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)$$

q: A prism has a regular hexagonal base with side 6 cm. If the total surface area of prism is 216√3 cm 2 , then what is the height (in cm) of prism?

q: Water is flowing at the rate of 5 km/h through a pipe of diameter 14 cm into a rectangular tank which is 50 m long 44 m wide. The time taken (in hours) for the rise in the level of water in the tank to be 7 cm is

q: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal tank are 3 m 2 , 12 m 2 and 16 m 2 . The capacity of the tank, in litres is:

q: The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle. If the lateral surface area and volume are 120 cm 2 , 40√3 cm 3 respectively then the side of base of the prism is

(i) Volume of prism = 40√3 Area of base × height = 40√3 $$\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}$$ (side) 2 × height = 40√3 (side) 2 × height = $$= \frac{{40\sqrt 3 \times 4}}{{\sqrt 3 }}$$ = 160 . . . . . (ii) Dividing equation (ii) by equation (i) $$\frac{{{{\left( {{\text{side}}} \right)}^2} \times {\text{height}}}}{{{\text{side}} \times {\text{height}}}} = \frac{{160}}{{40}}$$ side = 4 cm

q: A solid cube is cut into three cuboids of same volumes. What is the ratio of the surface area of the cube to the sum of the surface areas of any two of the cuboids so formed?

q: A ball of lead 4 cm in diameter is covered with gold. If the volume of the gold and lead are equal, then the thickness of gold (given $$\sqrt[3]2$$ = 1.259) is approximately

q: A right triangle with sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm is rotated about the side of 9 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
The volume of a right circular cone is 1232 cm 3 and its vertical height is 24 cm. Its curved surface area is

q: A hollow cylindrical tube 20 cm long is made of iron and its external and internal diameters are 8 cm and 6 cm respectively. The volume of iron used in making the tube is $$\left( {\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)$$

q: A solid cone of height 9 cm with diameter of its base 18 cm is cut out from a wooden solid sphere of radius 9 cm. The percentage of wood wasted is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Volume of sphere}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi {r^3} \\ & = \frac{4}{3}\pi {\left( 9 \right)^3} \\ & = 972\pi {\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & {\text{Volume of cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \frac{1}{3}\pi {\left( 9 \right)^2}9 \\ & = 243\pi {\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & \Rightarrow \% {\text{ of wasted wood}} \\ & = \frac{{\left( {972 - 243} \right)\pi }}{{972\pi }} \times 100 \\ & = 75\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio of weights of two spheres of different materials is 8 : 17 and the ratio of weights per 1 cc of materials of each is 289 : 64. The ratio of radii of the two spheres is

q: The base of a right prism is a trapezium. The length of the parallel sides are 8 cm and 14 cm and the distance between the parallel sides is 8 cm. If the volume of the prism is 1056 cm 3 , then the height of the prism is

q: A right angled sector of radius $$r$$ cm is rolled up into a cone in such a way that the two binding radii are joined together. Then the curved surface area of the cone is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {\text{Circumference of sectors}} = \frac{{\pi r}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{Circumference of base of cone of radius}} = 2\pi {r_1} \\ & \frac{{\pi r}}{2} = 2\pi {r_1} \Rightarrow {r_1} = \frac{r}{4} \\ & \therefore {\text{Radius of cone}} = \frac{r}{4} \\ & {\text{Curved surface area of cone}} = \pi {r_1}l \\ & l = {\text{slant height}} \\ & l = r \\ & \therefore {\text{Surface area of cone}} = \pi \times \frac{r}{4} \times r \Rightarrow \frac{{\pi {r^2}}}{4} \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of the largest possible rod that can be placed in a cubical room is 35√3 m. The surface area of the largest possible sphere that fit within the cubical room $$\left( {{\text{assuming }}\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)$$ (in sq. m) is

q: A sphere is placed in a cube so that it touches all the faces of the cube. If 'a' is the ratio of the volume of the cube to the volume of the sphere, and 'b' is the ratio of the surface area of the sphere to the surface area of the cube, then the value of ab is:

q: The external and the internal radii of a hollow right circular cylinder of height 15 cm are 6.75 cm and 5.25 cm respectively. If it is melted to form a solid cylinder of height half of the original cylinder, then the radius of the solid cylinder is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Volume of cylinder}} = \pi r_1^2h - \pi r_2^2h \\ & = \pi h\left( {r_1^2 - r_2^2} \right) \\ & = \pi h\left( {{r_1} + {r_2}} \right)\left( {{r_1} - {r_2}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 15 \times \left( {6.75 + 5.25} \right)\left( {6.75 - 5.25} \right) \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 15 \times 12 \times 1.5 \\ & {\text{Volume}} = \pi r_3^2\frac{h}{2} = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 15 \times 12 \times 1.5 \\ & r_3^2 \times \frac{{15}}{2} = 15 \times 12 \times 1.5 \\ & {r_3} = 6 \end{aligned}$$

q: A 22.5 m high tent is in the shape of a frustum of a cone surmounted by a hemisphere. If the diameters of the upper and the lower circular ends of the frustum are 21 m and 39 m, respectively, then find the area of cloth (in m 2 ) used to make the tent (ignoring the wastage). $$\left( {{\text{Use }}\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)$$
s: $$\begin{aligned} & r = \frac{{21}}{2} \\ & R = \frac{{39}}{2} \\ & {\text{Curved serface area of Hemisphere}} \\ & = 2\pi {r^2} \\ & = 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{21 \times 21}}{{2 \times 2}} \\ & = 693\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & H = \left( {22.5 - 10.5} \right) = 12{\text{ cm}} \\ & {L^2} = {H^2} + {\left( {R - r} \right)^2} \\ & {L^2} = {12^2} + {\left( {\frac{{39}}{2} - \frac{{21}}{2}} \right)^2} \\ & {L^2} = 144 + 81 \\ & L = \sqrt {225} \\ & L = 15{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{Curved serface area of Frustum of cone}} \\ & = \pi l\left( {R + r} \right) \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 15 \times \left[ {\left( {\frac{{39}}{2}} \right) + \left( {\frac{{21}}{2}} \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 15 \times 30 \\ & = \frac{{9900}}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 1414\frac{2}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & \therefore {\text{Total area of cloth}} \\ & = \left( {693 + 1414\frac{2}{7}} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 2107\frac{2}{7}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: Assume that a drop of water is spherical and its diameter is one-tenth of a cm. A conical glass has a height equal to the diameter of its rim. If 32,000 drops of water fill the glass completely. Then the height of the glass (in cm) is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Radius of water drop}} = \frac{1}{{20}}{\text{ cm}} \\ & {\text{Volume of a sphere}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times \frac{1}{{20}} \times \frac{1}{{20}} \times \frac{1}{{20}} \\ & {\text{Let the radius of cone}} = R \\ & {\text{Height}} = 2R \\ & {\text{According to question}} \\ & \frac{1}{3}\pi \times R \times R \times 2R = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times \frac{1}{{20}} \times \frac{1}{{20}} \times \frac{1}{{20}} \\ & {R^3} = \frac{{2 \times 32000}}{{20 \times 20 \times 20}} \\ & {R^3} = \frac{{64000}}{{20 \times 20 \times 20}} \\ & {R^3} = \frac{{40 \times 40 \times 40}}{{20 \times 20 \times 20}} \\ & R = \frac{{40}}{{20}} \\ & R = 2 \\ & {\text{Height of glass}} = 2R = 2 \times 2 = 4{\text{ cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Balls of marbles of diameter 1.4 cm are dropped into a cylindrical beaker containing some water and fully submerged. The diameter of the beaker is 7 cm. Find how many marbles have been dropped in it if the water rises by 5.6 cm?
s: Diameter of beaker = 7 cm Radius = $$\frac{7}{2}$$ cm Level of water rises = 5.6 cm Diameter of a marble = 1.4 cm ∴ Radius = $$\frac{{1.4}}{2}$$ = 0.7 cm Let n marbles are dropped so, Volume of n marbles $$= n \times \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( {0.7} \right)^3}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow n \times \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( {0.7} \right)^3} = n \times {\left( {\frac{7}{2}} \right)^2} \times 5.6 \\ & \Rightarrow n \times \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{7}{{10}} \times \frac{7}{{10}} \times \frac{7}{{10}} = \frac{7}{2} \times \frac{7}{2} \times \frac{{56}}{{10}} \\ & \Rightarrow n = 150 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 2.5 decimetre (dm), then its surface area increases by 110 dm 2 . What is the volume (in dm 3 ) of the sphere? $$\left( {{\text{take }}\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)$$

q: A conical tent has to accommodate 25 persons. Each person must have 4 m 2 of space on the ground and 80 m 3 of air to breathe. Find the height of the tent.
